method: Desk-screen expansion of the three district starting themes. A category is included if its trigger matches a theme; overlapping categories are deduplicated by ID. This is an assessment checklist, not additional district research, a severity ranking or evidence that a problem occurs at a site. Confirmed problems, impacts and budgets remain unassessed, not zero.

indicators.title: People and households
indicators.measure: Unique direct people; unique households; disaggregate by age, gender, disability and livelihood where consent allows.
indicators.method: Count only people with documented access to the improved service. Deduplicate across projects; report indirect reach separately.

indicators.title: Livestock
indicators.measure: Animals by species; households owning them; animal-days with adequate water, shade or fodder; morbidity and mortality.
indicators.method: Use owner registers and veterinary records. Animals are not people; do not add them into a single beneficiary total.
indicators.timing: Baseline and same heat/dry season after delivery

indicators.title: Trees and habitat
indicators.measure: Existing trees protected; planted native trees; surviving trees at 12 and 36 months; canopy and habitat area (ha).
indicators.method: Keep planted and surviving counts separate. Record species, plot, survival denominator and replacement trees. Avoid planting in natural grasslands or wetlands.

indicators.title: Lakes, tanks and wetlands
indicators.measure: Unique waterbodies; area (ha); surveyed capacity (m³); seasonal water levels; quality; functioning inlets/outlets; habitat.
indicators.method: Assign a stable waterbody ID. Count restoration only against agreed ecological and service criteria; desilting volume is not automatically water saved.
indicators.timing: Wet/dry baseline and comparable post-work seasons

indicators.title: Water security
indicators.measure: People receiving safe water; service days; quality test compliance; groundwater depth; verified storage and abstraction (m³).
indicators.method: Use laboratory results, service logs and calibrated meters; separate drinking water, irrigation and recharge. A lined pond is storage, not a recharge structure.
indicators.timing: Monthly service logs; seasonal levels and quality

indicators.title: Farms and livelihoods
indicators.measure: Unique farmers; hectares treated; yield, net farm income, irrigation use and crop loss.
indicators.method: Compare equivalent crop seasons and weather; include input/labour costs and a suitable comparison group where feasible.
indicators.timing: Baseline and at least two comparable crop seasons

indicators.title: Heat and buildings
indicators.measure: Unique occupants; roofs treated (m²); occupied hours above an agreed heat threshold; indoor/outdoor temperature; illness.
indicators.method: Paired sensors and occupancy records; distinguish room temperature from roof-surface temperature. Do not promise a fixed temperature reduction.

indicators.title: Floods, slopes and coasts
indicators.measure: Households and critical assets exposed; flood depth/duration; warning lead time; evacuation access; erosion or slope movement.
indicators.method: Map exposure and drainage/catchment effects. Risk reduction is modelled until comparable events occur; disclose model assumptions.
indicators.timing: Baseline, annual preparedness and after relevant events

indicators.title: Energy and emissions
indicators.measure: Metered kWh; equipment uptime; verified fuel displaced; tCO₂e with dated emission factors.
indicators.method: Separate generation, consumption and export; state boundary and factor. Never infer carbon sequestration from tree count alone.

problems.title: Flood exposure of homes and services
Sewage and nutrient loads into waterbodies
Lost tank, wetland or flood-storage function
Storm warnings and safe evacuation gaps
Slope instability near settlements and roads
Unsafe hill drainage or disturbed slopes
Crop water stress and irrigation inefficiency
Soil erosion and declining soil cover
Loss of native canopy and poor restoration survival
